views.name: patient_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ID,
  SEX,
  Birthday,
  "Description",
  "First Date",
  Admission,
  Diagnosis
FROM
  Patient

params.description: Canonical one-row-per-patient core record exposing demographic and index encounter fields from the Patient table.
params.when_to_use: Look up patient-level attributes (sex, birthday, textual description). | Use as the patient dimension when joining patient-level measures to other patient-scoped aggregates. | Compose patient-level filters (e.g., by sex or birthdate range) before joining with event-level tables. | Serve as the driving table for analytics that require one row per patient (e.g., counts of patients, join to latest-lab-per-patient).
params.output_schema: ID: patient identifier — derived directly from Patient.ID | SEX: patient sex/gender code or value — derived directly from Patient.SEX | Birthday: patient date of birth — derived directly from Patient.Birthday | Description: textual description field from patient record — derived directly from Patient."Description" | First Date: a date/timestamp field (named "First Date") from patient record — derived directly from Patient."First Date" | Admission: admission date/time or admission-related field from patient record — derived directly from Patient.Admission | Diagnosis: diagnosis text/code stored on the patient record — derived directly from Patient.Diagnosis
params.grounded_columns: Patient.ID | Patient.SEX | Patient.Birthday | Patient."Description" | Patient."First Date" | Patient.Admission | Patient.Diagnosis
params.metric: No derived metrics are computed in this view. All output columns are direct projections of base columns (no aggregates or expressions).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to patient-level or one-row-per-patient views/tables on ID — safe because patient_core is one-row-per-ID so measures/attributes from patient_core will not be duplicated. Examples: join to lab_latest_per_patient on ID (one-row-per-patient) or patients_with_recent_exam_rank on ID (if that sibling view is one-row-per-patient). | Do NOT directly join patient_core to one-to-many event tables (e.g., examination_events, laboratory_records, examination_counts_per_patient if it is per-event) without re-aggregating the event-side first, because joining to multi-row-per-patient tables will duplicate patient_core rows and multiply any patient-level measures. If you need aggregated event measures per patient, join patient_core to an aggregated view that is explicitly one-row-per-patient (e.g., lab_aggregates_per_patient, examination_counts_per_patient if documented as AGG producing one row per patient). | When composing with ranked or windowed sibling views (e.g., lab_latest_per_patient, patients_with_recent_exam_rank), confirm those sibling views' declared grain is one-row-per-patient before joining on ID; safe joins require the other side to also be one-row-per-patient or to be pre-aggregated/filtered to a single row per ID. | If you need to combine patient_core with event-level details (examination_events, laboratory_records), either: (a) aggregate the event table to patient-level first (e.g., counts, max/min dates) and then join on ID; or (b) keep the join but be aware that the result will be one row per event and you must not treat patient_core's values as independent patient-level aggregates without re-aggregation. | Joining to reshaped or join-mode sibling views (patients_with_exams_and_lab_counts, patient_with_latest_lab, exams_with_same_day_lab) is permitted only when you verify their declared grain: if they are one-row-per-patient (or one-row-per-ID) the join is safe; if they are many-to-one or many-to-many, re-aggregate first to patient level to avoid measure duplication.

views.description: Normalized patient-level projection exposing stable demographic and identifying columns. Use this as the patient entity when joining to facts or computing per-patient aggregates. | Use for: List patients by demographic attributes (SEX, Birthday range); Join patient info to latest lab or examination; Aggregate counts of patients by Admission or Diagnosis

List the patient ID, sex and birthday of patient with LDH beyond normal range.
For patients with severe degree of thrombosis, list their ID, sex and disease the patient is diagnosed with.
Provide all ID, sex and birthday of patients whose urea nitrogen (UN) just within the borderline of passing?

views.name: examination_events
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ID,
  "Examination Date",
  "aCL IgG",
  "aCL IgM",
  ANA,
  "ANA Pattern",
  "aCL IgA",
  Diagnosis,
  KCT,
  RVVT,
  LAC,
  Symptoms,
  Thrombosis
FROM
  Examination

params.description: Provides one row per Examination record (ID, Examination Date) with a set of lab/result fields and diagnosis/symptom flags for that examination.
params.when_to_use: Fetch the values of specific examination-level measurements and findings for an individual examination (by ID) or for examinations in a date range. | Compose patient-level timelines or event sequences by joining examination rows to patient or lab views on patient ID and/or exam date. | Build aggregates that count or summarize examination-level findings (e.g., how many examinations had positive LAC) after appropriate re-aggregation.
params.output_schema: ID: unique identifier of the examination record, derived directly from Examination.ID | Examination Date: date/time of the examination, derived directly from Examination."Examination Date" | aCL IgG: value or result for anticardiolipin IgG measured at this examination, derived from Examination."aCL IgG" | aCL IgM: value or result for anticardiolipin IgM measured at this examination, derived from Examination."aCL IgM" | ANA: antinuclear antibody (ANA) result for this examination, derived from Examination.ANA | ANA Pattern: ANA staining pattern recorded at this examination, derived from Examination."ANA Pattern" | aCL IgA: value or result for anticardiolipin IgA measured at this examination, derived from Examination."aCL IgA" | Diagnosis: diagnosis assigned/recorded for this examination, derived from Examination.Diagnosis | KCT: KCT test result recorded for this examination, derived from Examination.KCT | RVVT: Russell viper venom test result for this examination, derived from Examination.RVVT | LAC: lupus anticoagulant (LAC) result for this examination, derived from Examination.LAC | Symptoms: symptoms recorded at this examination, derived from Examination.Symptoms | Thrombosis: thrombosis flag or detail recorded at this examination, derived from Examination.Thrombosis
params.grounded_columns: Examination.ID | Examination."Examination Date" | Examination."aCL IgG" | Examination."aCL IgM" | Examination.ANA | Examination."ANA Pattern" | Examination."aCL IgA" | Examination.Diagnosis | Examination.KCT | Examination.RVVT | Examination.LAC | Examination.Symptoms | Examination.Thrombosis
params.metric: ID = direct base column (no aggregation) -> Examination.ID | Examination Date = direct base column (no aggregation) -> Examination."Examination Date" | aCL IgG = direct base column (no aggregation) -> Examination."aCL IgG" | aCL IgM = direct base column (no aggregation) -> Examination."aCL IgM" | ANA = direct base column (no aggregation) -> Examination.ANA | ANA Pattern = direct base column (no aggregation) -> Examination."ANA Pattern" | aCL IgA = direct base column (no aggregation) -> Examination."aCL IgA" | Diagnosis = direct base column (no aggregation) -> Examination.Diagnosis | KCT = direct base column (no aggregation) -> Examination.KCT | RVVT = direct base column (no aggregation) -> Examination.RVVT | LAC = direct base column (no aggregation) -> Examination.LAC | Symptoms = direct base column (no aggregation) -> Examination.Symptoms | Thrombosis = direct base column (no aggregation) -> Examination.Thrombosis
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to patient_core (or any patient-dimension view) on ID -> patient_core.ID — safe because this view is one row per Examination.ID (the examination primary key) so joining to patient metadata (one row per patient) will not duplicate examination rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to lab_latest_per_patient or lab_aggregates_per_patient on ID -> lab_* views keyed by patient ID are safe only if those lab views return one row per patient and you join by patient ID (not by examination date). Joining on patient ID to a one-row-per-patient view will not duplicate examination rows. | do NOT join directly to laboratory_records (raw lab records) on patient ID or on (ID, date) if laboratory_records is one-to-many per examination or patient: such a join would multiply examination rows and duplicate the examination-level fields. Instead, first aggregate laboratory_records to one row per examination (or per patient) (for example, using lab_aggregates_per_patient or lab_latest_per_patient) and then join. | do NOT join to exams_with_same_day_lab or other JOIN/RESHAPE sibling views without checking their grain: if the sibling view expands examinations to multiple rows per Examination.ID (e.g., pairing with multiple lab records on same day), joining will duplicate measures from this view. To preserve correctness, either (a) aggregate the joined view back to one row per Examination.ID before combining, or (b) join in a subquery that groups the many-side and reduces to the same grain. | When composing patient-level metrics (counts, rates) from this view's columns, re-aggregate after joins: e.g., to count examinations with positive LAC per patient, group by patient ID and use COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE LAC = 'positive') or SUM(CASE WHEN LAC = 'positive' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) over the examination rows — do not rely on joining to a many-side without aggregation as that will overcount. | If joining on Examination."Examination Date" to time-aligned lab windows (e.g., lab records within +/- N days), ensure the lab side is reduced to one row per examination (e.g., choose latest/closest lab per exam) before joining, otherwise multiple matching lab rows will duplicate the examination row.

views.description: One row per clinical Examination event for a patient, exposing examination date, test results, diagnosis and binary flags. Use this to filter cohorts by examination attributes or to join to patient-level data. | Use for: Find examinations with thrombosis or specific symptom/diagnosis; Trend of aCL/ANA measures across examinations; Count examinations per patient or filter by exam date ranges

For patients with severe degree of thrombosis, list their ID, sex and disease the patient is diagnosed with.

params.grounded_columns: Laboratory.ID | Laboratory.Date | Laboratory.GOT | Laboratory.GPT | Laboratory.LDH | Laboratory.ALP | Laboratory.TP | Laboratory.ALB | Laboratory.UA | Laboratory.UN | Laboratory.CRE | Laboratory."T-BIL" | Laboratory."T-CHO" | Laboratory.TG | Laboratory.CPK | Laboratory.GLU | Laboratory.WBC | Laboratory.RBC | Laboratory.HGB | Laboratory.HCT | Laboratory.PLT | Laboratory.PT | Laboratory.APTT | Laboratory.FG | Laboratory.PIC | Laboratory.TAT | Laboratory.TAT2 | Laboratory."U-PRO" | Laboratory.IGG | Laboratory.IGA | Laboratory.IGM | Laboratory.CRP | Laboratory.RA | Laboratory.RF | Laboratory.C3 | Laboratory.C4 | Laboratory.RNP | Laboratory.SM | Laboratory.SC170 | Laboratory.SSA | Laboratory.SSB | Laboratory.CENTROMEA | Laboratory.DNA | Laboratory."DNA-II"
params.metric: No derived aggregates are computed in this view; all output columns are direct column projections from the Laboratory table: output_col = Laboratory.<column> (see grounded_columns).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to patient_core on laboratory_records.ID = patient_core.ID — safe because laboratory_records is one row per (ID, Date) and patient_core is expected to be one row per patient ID; this join will not duplicate lab measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to lab_latest_per_patient on (laboratory_records.ID = lab_latest_per_patient.ID AND laboratory_records.Date = lab_latest_per_patient.Date) — safe because lab_latest_per_patient should identify a single latest lab row per patient and matching by both ID and Date preserves one-to-one mapping. | do NOT join laboratory_records directly to any one-to-many detail tables (for example: examinations/events that may have multiple rows per (ID, Date) or other aggregated-per-exam tables) without pre-aggregation or keys that guarantee one-row matching — doing so will multiply laboratory_records rows and thus duplicate its measured values. | If you need to combine with examinations that are one-to-many per lab row, either (a) aggregate the exam-side measures to the (ID, Date) grain prior to joining (e.g., COUNT, MIN, MAX per ID+Date), or (b) join on a unique exam identifier available on both sides (ensuring a one-to-one mapping). | When composing higher-level patient metrics (e.g., latest value per patient, average over time), use grouping/aggregation on laboratory_records at the ID level (or ID+timewindow) rather than joining to lower-grain tables which would require re-aggregation to avoid double-counting. | Examples of safe composition using sibling views: join to lab_aggregates_per_patient or lab_running_avg_by_patient only when the sibling view is aggregated to ID (one row per patient) — joining laboratory_records to a one-row-per-patient aggregate will duplicate that aggregate across the lab rows unless you join on ID and then purposefully select the aggregate (understand duplication). Prefer deriving aggregates from laboratory_records directly or using the sibling pre-aggregated views depending on desired grain.

views.description: One row per Laboratory measurement date for a patient, exposing core lab measures and immunologic markers. Use this as the base time-series of labs to filter by date, compute aggregates, or join to examinations with date-matching logic. | Use for: Per-patient time series of lab values; Aggregate lab statistics per patient (mean/max/min) over a period; Match lab records to examinations by date

SELECT

  GOT,

  LDH,
  ALP,
  TP,
  ALB,
  UA,

params.when_to_use: Get the latest lab values for each patient as-of the latest Date recorded in Laboratory. | Compose patient-level analyses that need the most recent lab snapshot (e.g., current biomarkers, flagging abnormal last result). | Join latest lab results to patient demographic or exam data without duplicating lab measures if joined correctly on patient ID.

directly from Laboratory.FG | PIC: Plasmin-alpha2-plasmin inhibitor complex; directly from Laboratory.PIC | TAT: Thrombin-antithrombin complex (TAT); directly from Laboratory.TAT | TAT2: Secondary TAT field; directly from Laboratory.TAT2 | U-PRO: Urine protein; directly from Laboratory."U-PRO" | IGG: Immunoglobulin G; directly from Laboratory.IGG | IGA: Immunoglobulin A; directly from Laboratory.IGA | IGM: Immunoglobulin M; directly from Laboratory.DNA | DNA-II: Anti-DNA-II antibody; directly from Laboratory."DNA-II" | lab_row_rank: row number ranking labs per patient by Date descending (1 = most recent); computed as ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ID ORDER BY Date DESC)

views.description: Latest Laboratory record per patient based on Date. Exposes a row_number rank and returns the most recent lab row (rank = 1) when filtered downstream. Useful for snapshotting current lab state per patient. | Use for: Get latest lab snapshot per patient (WHERE lab_row_rank = 1); Ranked lab history queries (top-K recent lab dates per patient)

views.name: examination_counts_per_patient
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ID,
  COUNT(*) AS exam_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN Thrombosis IS NOT NULL AND Thrombosis != 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS thrombosis_count,
  MIN("Examination Date") AS first_exam_date,
  MAX("Examination Date") AS last_exam_date
FROM
  Examination
GROUP BY
  ID

params.description: Per-patient aggregate counts and exam date range summarizing Examination rows per patient ID.
params.when_to_use: Get total number of examinations per patient | Get number of examinations with recorded thrombosis per patient | Find each patient’s first and last examination dates | Join patient-level exam summary into patient-level analyses without re-scanning the Examination table | Compose with other patient-level aggregates (e.g., labs) to build combined patient summaries
params.output_schema: ID: patient identifier, derived from Examination.ID (grouping key) | exam_count: total number of Examination rows for that ID, derived from COUNT(*) over Examination grouped by ID | thrombosis_count: count of Examination rows for that ID where Thrombosis is not NULL and not equal to 0, derived from SUM(CASE WHEN Thrombosis IS NOT NULL AND Thrombosis != 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) over Examination grouped by ID | first_exam_date: earliest Examination."Examination Date" for that ID, derived from MIN("Examination Date") over Examination grouped by ID | last_exam_date: latest Examination."Examination Date" for that ID, derived from MAX("Examination Date") over Examination grouped by ID
params.grounded_columns: Examination.ID | Examination.Thrombosis | Examination."Examination Date"
params.metric: exam_count = COUNT(*) /* count of Examination rows per Examination.ID */ | thrombosis_count = SUM(CASE WHEN Examination.Thrombosis IS NOT NULL AND Examination.Thrombosis != 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) /* count of exams with thrombosis per ID */ | first_exam_date = MIN(Examination."Examination Date") /* earliest exam date per ID */ | last_exam_date = MAX(Examination."Examination Date") /* latest exam date per ID */
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to patient_core on ID — safe because patient_core is one-row-per-patient and this view is one-row-per-patient (ID); joining preserves measures without duplication | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to lab_latest_per_patient on ID — safe because lab_latest_per_patient is one-row-per-patient (ID) and joining will not multiply exam_count/thrombosis_count | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to lab_aggregates_per_patient on ID — safe because lab_aggregates_per_patient is aggregated to one row per patient; measures remain correct | do NOT join directly to examination_events (one-to-many) without re-aggregation — examination_events contains multiple rows per ID and would multiply exam_count/thrombosis_count unless you re-aggregate or join on a one-row-per-exam key and then re-summarize | do NOT join directly to laboratory_records (one-to-many) without re-aggregation — laboratory_records is many per patient and will duplicate the exam metrics; instead aggregate labs to patient level first (e.g., lab_aggregates_per_patient) or join using EXISTS/semi-join logic | when composing with sibling AGG or RANK views (e.g., lab_aggregates_per_patient, patients_with_recent_exam_rank), ensure the other side is one-row-per-ID or re-aggregate after joining to avoid double-counting | if you need patient+exam-level analytics (one row per exam), join this view only to a single exam row (e.g., examination_events filtered to a single event) and avoid joining raw multi-row exam sets, because exam_count is already an aggregate across all exams | if joining to views that are at a different grain (e.g., lab running windows, per-exam-lab joins like exams_with_same_day_lab), either (a) aggregate those views to patient-level before joining, or (b) join and then re-aggregate exam_count/thrombosis_count using SUM(DISTINCT ...) or recompute from Examination to ensure correctness

views.description: Per-patient aggregate counts and basic summary of examinations: total number of examinations and number of examinations with Thrombosis flagged. Useful for patient-level risk summaries. | Use for: Count examinations per patient; Identify patients with any thrombosis events; Find patients' first and last examination dates

views.name: lab_aggregates_per_patient
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ID,
  AVG(GOT) AS avg_GOT,
  MIN(GOT) AS min_GOT,
  MAX(GOT) AS max_GOT,
  AVG(GPT) AS avg_GPT,
  MIN(GPT) AS min_GPT,
  MAX(GPT) AS max_GPT,
  AVG(LDH) AS avg_LDH,
  MIN(LDH) AS min_LDH,
  MAX(LDH) AS max_LDH,
  AVG(ALP) AS avg_ALP,
  MIN(ALP) AS min_ALP,
  MAX(ALP) AS max_ALP,
  AVG(WBC) AS avg_WBC,
  MIN(WBC) AS min_WBC,
  MAX(WBC) AS max_WBC,
  AVG(HGB) AS avg_HGB,
  MIN(HGB) AS min_HGB,
  MAX(HGB) AS max_HGB,
  AVG(PLT) AS avg_PLT,
  MIN(PLT) AS min_PLT,
  MAX(PLT) AS max_PLT
FROM
  Laboratory

views.name: patient_with_latest_lab

  l.WBC,
  l.HGB,
  l.PLT,
  l.CRP,
  l."DNA-II"
FROM
  patient_core p

params.description: For each patient (ID) return demographic fields plus that patient's single latest lab row (the lab row with lab_row_rank = 1) and its lab values.

Doing so does not multiply rows because there is at most one latest lab row per patient. | Do NOT join this view directly to any one-to-many table (for example: laboratory_records, examination_events, exams_with_same_day_lab, or other raw events) without aggregation or de-duplication on the many-side first — because those joins will multiply the per-patient rows and therefore duplicate the latest-lab measures (e.g., joining to laboratory_records which has many rows per patient will produce multiple copies of the latest lab values). | If you need to combine with one-to-many detail (exams, raw labs), either: (a) aggregate the detail to one row per patient (or per patient+date) before joining; or (b) join and then re-aggregate (e.g., compute SUM/AVG after the join) ensuring you use appropriate GROUP BY patient_with_latest_lab.ID to avoid measure inflation. | When joining to other patient-level aggregates (examination_counts_per_patient, lab_aggregates_per_patient, patients_with_recent_exam_rank), joining on ID is safe because those sibling views are also intended as patient-level summaries (one row per ID). params.description: Pairs each Examination row with Laboratory results taken on the same date for the same patient — answers questions about exam findings together with same-day lab values.

params.grounded_columns: Examination.ID | Examination."Examination Date" | Examination."aCL IgG" | Examination."aCL IgM" | Examination.ANA | Examination."ANA Pattern" | Examination."aCL IgA" | Examination.Diagnosis | Examination.KCT | Examination.RVVT | Examination.LAC | Examination.Symptoms | Examination.Thrombosis | Laboratory.ID | Laboratory.Date | Laboratory.GOT | Laboratory.GPT | Laboratory.LDH | Laboratory.ALP | Laboratory.TP | Laboratory.ALB | Laboratory.WBC | Laboratory.HGB | Laboratory.PLT
params.metric: This view is at a row-grain of (Examination.ID, Examination."Examination Date", Laboratory.Date) as produced by the equality join on ID and date. There are no aggregated measures in the SELECT — all output columns are direct passthroughs from the underlying tables. | Derived/renamed column: Examination_Diagnosis = Examination.Diagnosis (simple projection). | Derived/renamed column: Lab_Date = Laboratory.Date (simple projection).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to patient_core (or any one-row-per-patient dimension) on ID — safe because patient_core has at most one row per patient (ID), so adding patient attributes will not duplicate exam+lab rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to patient_with_latest_lab on (ID, Lab_Date) only if patient_with_latest_lab is guaranteed one row per (ID, Lab_Date). Verify sibling view semantics before joining; if it is one-row-per-patient (latest lab only), join on ID only. | do NOT join directly to laboratory_records (a one-to-many table of lab records) on ID without also joining/aggregating by Laboratory.Date = Lab_Date, because laboratory_records may contain multiple lab result rows per (ID, Date) or additional lab tests per date. Joining without re-aggregation can multiply rows and duplicate measures. | do NOT join to examination_events (a one-to-many events view) on ID only without matching Examination Date, because there may be multiple examinations per patient; joining on ID alone duplicates this view's exam-level rows. | When you need to combine with sibling AGG views (examination_counts_per_patient, lab_aggregates_per_patient): join on ID (and possibly date range) but do not join an aggregate that is at patient-level to this exam-level view without using an appropriate key or applying non-duplicating aggregation (e.g., aggregate this view up to patient first, or use a safe join on ID where the aggregate is one-row-per-ID). | If composing further time-based analyses (e.g., windowing or running averages), prefer the lab_running_avg_by_patient view or compute aggregates over this view partitioned by ID and ordered by Examination Date; ensure joins to other time-series views align on both ID and date to avoid multiplicity. | Guiding rule: treat this view as event-level (patient + examination date with the lab on that same date). views.name: lab_running_avg_by_patient
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ID,
  Date,
  WBC,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ID ORDER BY Date) AS seq_num,
  AVG(WBC) OVER (PARTITION BY ID ORDER BY Date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_avg_WBC
FROM
  Laboratory

params.description: Per-patient, per-date running average of white blood cell (WBC) measurements and the sequential observation number for that patient.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve the running (cumulative) average WBC for each laboratory observation for a patient over time. | Build time-series analyses that require the cumulative mean of WBC up to each date per patient. | Compose further aggregations by patient (e.g., final running average, mean of running averages) without recomputing window logic. | Join to patient or event dimensions when you need one row per laboratory observation with its running average and sequence number.

params.grounded_columns: Laboratory.ID | Laboratory.Date | Laboratory.WBC

views.name: patients_with_exams_and_lab_counts
views.body_sql:

  p.ID,
  COALESCE(e.exam_count, 0) AS exam_count,
  COALESCE(l.lab_count, 0) AS lab_count
FROM
  Patient p
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT ID, COUNT(*) AS exam_count FROM Examination GROUP BY ID
  ) e ON p.ID = e.ID
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT ID, COUNT(*) AS lab_count FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID
  ) l ON p.ID = l.ID

params.description: Per-patient counts of examinations and laboratory records (one row per Patient.ID).

params.grounded_columns: Patient.ID | Examination.ID | Laboratory.ID
params.metric: exam_count = COALESCE(e.exam_count, 0) where e.exam_count = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Examination WHERE Examination.ID = Patient.ID GROUP BY Examination.ID) | lab_count = COALESCE(l.lab_count, 0) where l.lab_count = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Laboratory WHERE Laboratory.ID = Patient.ID GROUP BY Laboratory.ID)

If they are rank/window outputs that can contain multiple rows per ID, aggregate or select the single intended row before joining. | when combining measures (e.g., counting patients with recent labs), perform patient-level aggregation after joins to maintain correct cardinality: first join patient_latest_lab_date to patient-level dimension(s) that are one-row-per-patient, then apply COUNT/DISTINCT or other aggregates at the patient grain rather than relying on pre-joined detail rows.

views.name: laboratory_measurements_raw

views.name: patient_basic_demographics

SELECT
  p.ID AS ID,
  p.SEX AS SEX,
  p.Birthday AS Birthday,
  CASE
    WHEN p.Birthday IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(strftime('%Y', p.Birthday) AS INTEGER)
  END AS birth_year,
  CASE WHEN p.Birthday IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS birthday_present
FROM
  patient_core p

params.description: Provides one-row-per-patient basic demographic fields (sex and birthday/year presence) for use as a stable patient dimension.
params.when_to_use: Look up a patient's sex or birthday information by patient ID | Join patient demographics into analyses that aggregate by patient (e.g., counts by birth_year or sex) | Filter cohorts by presence of a recorded birthday (birthday_present) or by birth_year | Compose higher-level patient-level metrics that require patient attributes as non-duplicating dimension data

params.grounded_columns: patient_core.ID | patient_core.SEX | patient_core.Birthday
params.metric: birth_year = CASE WHEN patient_core.Birthday IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(strftime('%Y', patient_core.Birthday) AS INTEGER) END | birthday_present = CASE WHEN patient_core.Birthday IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension or one-row-per-patient views/tables (e.g., patient_core) on ID — safe because patient_basic_demographics is one row per patient ID so its attributes will not be duplicated. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many event/measurement tables or views without re-aggregation (e.g., examination_events, laboratory_records, exam counts, lab_aggregates_per_patient) on ID because those are multi-row per patient and will multiply patient_basic_demographics rows and thus duplicate any patient-level measures unless you first aggregate the many-side to one row per patient (for example, SUM/COUNT or latest-per-patient). | When combining with per-patient aggregates (examination_counts_per_patient, lab_aggregates_per_patient, lab_latest_per_patient, patient_with_latest_lab), join on ID is safe only if the other object is guaranteed to be one-row-per-patient (those named with AGG or RANK that are defined as per-patient should be verified). If the other side is one-row-per-patient, the join will not duplicate measures; if it is multi-row, aggregate or deduplicate the other side first. | If you need to attach many-side rows (exams, labs) and preserve per-event granularity, keep patient_basic_demographics as a dimension and accept multiplicity, or perform GROUP BY patient_basic_demographics.ID after joining while using aggregate functions to avoid duplicating patient-level flags. | Examples: safe -> JOIN patient_basic_demographics AS d ON d.ID = patient_core.ID (no duplication). Unsafe without re-aggregation -> JOIN patient_basic_demographics AS d ON d.ID = examination_events.patient_id (examination_events has multiple rows per patient) unless examination_events is first reduced (e.g., latest event per patient).

views.name: patient_examination_age_events
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  e."ID" AS "ID",
  e."Examination Date" AS "Examination Date",
  CAST(strftime('%Y', e."Examination Date") AS INTEGER) AS "Examination_year",
  p."Birthday" AS "Birthday",
  CAST(strftime('%Y', p."Birthday") AS INTEGER) AS "birth_year",
  (CAST(strftime('%Y', e."Examination Date") AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%Y', p."Birthday") AS INTEGER)) AS "age_at_exam"
FROM
  examination_events e
  JOIN patient_core p USING ("ID")
WHERE
  p."Birthday" IS NOT NULL

params.description: Provides patient-level examination events with patient birth date and computed age at each examination (one row per patient examination date).
params.when_to_use: Find a patient's age at the time of a specific examination date | Group or filter examination events by patient birth year or examination year | Build age-based cohorts or age-at-exam aggregates (when composed with safe aggregation) | Join examination events to other per-exam or per-patient facts while preserving correct age calculation

params.grounded_columns: examination_events."ID" | examination_events."Examination Date" | patient_core."ID" | patient_core."Birthday"
params.metric: Examination_year = CAST(strftime('%Y', examination_events."Examination Date") AS INTEGER) | birth_year = CAST(strftime('%Y', patient_core."Birthday") AS INTEGER) | age_at_exam = Examination_year - birth_year

Such joins will multiply rows and thus duplicate age_at_exam and any counts derived from this view. | If you need to bring in lab results that can be multiple per exam, pre-aggregate labs to the (ID, Examination Date) level (e.g., latest or aggregated metrics per exam) before joining; or join labs on both ID and Examination Date if lab rows are strictly one-per (ID, Examination Date). | When composing into higher-level aggregates (e.g., average age_at_exam per birth_year), perform the aggregation after joining any additional data and ensure you aggregate age_at_exam appropriately (e.g., AVG(age_at_exam) over the desired group) rather than relying on row multiplication. | Joining to pre-aggregated per-patient views (for example examination_counts_per_patient which is aggregated per patient) is safe if you only need per-patient aggregates; but be explicit about grain alignment: this view's grain is (ID, Examination Date), so joining a per-patient aggregate will replicate that aggregate across all exam rows for that patient unless you instead aggregate this view up to patient level first.

ON laboratory_rows_with_patient_id_and_hgb.ID = patient_core.ID) — safe because patient_core is one-row-per-patient (normalised patient dimension) so joining will not duplicate HGB rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to patient_demographic_admission on ID — safe if patient_demographic_admission is one-row-per-patient (or otherwise one-row-per-ID at the same patient grain), because it will not multiply HGB rows. | do NOT join directly to examination_events or any other one-to-many event table on ID without re-aggregation or deduplication first — those tables can have multiple rows per (ID, Date) and would multiply laboratory_rows_with_patient_id_and_hgb rows and duplicate HGB measures. | do NOT join directly to examination_counts_per_patient, lab_aggregates_per_patient, lab_running_avg_by_patient, lab_latest_per_patient or other aggregate/rank views unless you understand their grain: if those views are one-row-per-patient (or one-row-per-(ID,Date) matching this view) it is safe; if they are one-to-many relative to (ID,Date) you must aggregate or join on matching keys. views.name: laboratory_measurements
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "ID",
  "Date",
  "T-CHO",
  "GLU",
  "WBC",
  "HGB",
  "PLT"
FROM "Laboratory"

params.description: Patient-level laboratory measurement snapshot: one row per patient ID and Date with selected lab values (T-CHO, GLU, WBC, HGB, PLT).
params.when_to_use: Retrieve lab test values for a given patient and date (exact-match lookups). | Join patient demographics or encounter metadata to a specific lab event without double-counting lab values. | Compose additional aggregations or time-series calculations when starting from distinct (ID, Date) lab records. | Build features for modeling where each example is a single lab observation (patient-date) and you need these specific lab columns.
params.output_schema: ID: patient identifier — directly from Laboratory."ID" (grain column). | Date: lab event date — directly from Laboratory."Date" (grain column). | T-CHO: total cholesterol measurement value — directly from Laboratory."T-CHO". | GLU: glucose measurement value — directly from Laboratory."GLU". | WBC: white blood cell count measurement value — directly from Laboratory."WBC". | HGB: hemoglobin measurement value — directly from Laboratory."HGB". | PLT: platelet count measurement value — directly from Laboratory."PLT".
params.grounded_columns: Laboratory."ID" | Laboratory."Date" | Laboratory."T-CHO" | Laboratory."GLU" | Laboratory."WBC" | Laboratory."HGB" | Laboratory."PLT"
params.metric: T-CHO = Laboratory."T-CHO" (raw measurement, no aggregation) | GLU = Laboratory."GLU" (raw measurement, no aggregation) | WBC = Laboratory."WBC" (raw measurement, no aggregation) | HGB = Laboratory."HGB" (raw measurement, no aggregation) | PLT = Laboratory."PLT" (raw measurement, no aggregation)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to patient_core on ID — safe because patient_core is one-row-per-ID (joining on ID will not duplicate (ID, Date) rows). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to patient_demographic_admission on ID (or ID + admission keys if present) — safe only if that view is one-row-per-ID or per-admission and you join on matching unique keys; verify the sibling view's grain before joining. | DO NOT join directly to examination_events (one-to-many per patient) on ID without aggregation of examination_events first — joining would multiply laboratory rows for a single (ID, Date) and duplicate these measurement values. | DO NOT join directly to laboratory_records or any other one-to-many lab/event-level view on ID or Date without re-aggregation — those joins can produce repeated (ID, Date) combinations and therefore duplicate the raw measurement values. | Safe composition pattern for many-to-one joins: join laboratory_measurements (one-row-per ID+Date) to a dimension that is unique on ID or on (ID, Date) — e.g., patient_core (unique on ID) or lab_latest_per_patient (if joining on ID and you intend to filter to latest). | If you need to combine with one-to-many detail (examinations, multiple lab records), aggregate the detail first to a compatible grain (for example, counts or latest-per-(ID,Date) aggregates) and then join on (ID, Date) or ID so that measures from laboratory_measurements are not multiplied. | When composing higher-level metrics (per-patient aggregates across dates), first aggregate laboratory_measurements (e.g., AVG(T-CHO) GROUP BY ID) and then join that aggregated result to other tables — do not perform per-patient aggregation by joining this view to a one-to-many table and then aggregating without removing duplicates.

views.name: patient_monthly_lab_aggregates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ID,
  strftime('%Y-%m', Date) AS month,
  SUM("T-CHO") AS tcho_sum,
  SUM("GLU") AS glucose_sum,
  AVG("WBC") AS wbc_mean,
  AVG("HGB") AS hgb_mean,
  SUM("PLT") AS plt_sum
FROM
  Laboratory
GROUP BY
  ID,
  strftime('%Y-%m', Date)

params.description: Per-patient, per-month aggregates of selected laboratory test measures (sums and means) computed from the Laboratory table.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve total or average lab test values for each patient in a given month (e.g., monthly cholesterol sum, glucose sum, mean WBC and HGB, platelet sum). | Time-series or trend analyses at a monthly grain per patient (e.g., plot monthly glucose_sum for a patient). | Compose higher-level cohorts or joins that need one row per patient-month with pre-aggregated lab metrics (e.g., join to admissions or demographics at patient-month level). | As a building block for further aggregation (e.g., monthly-to-quarterly or patient-level summaries) or windowing operations that require a stable patient-month grain.
params.output_schema: ID: patient identifier — derived from Laboratory.ID (passed through unchanged in the view). | month: month string in YYYY-MM format — derived from strftime('%Y-%m', Laboratory.Date) used to group lab records into month buckets. | tcho_sum: sum of 'T-CHO' values for that patient in that month — derived from SUM(Laboratory."T-CHO"). | glucose_sum: sum of 'GLU' values for that patient in that month — derived from SUM(Laboratory."GLU"). | wbc_mean: average of 'WBC' values for that patient in that month — derived from AVG(Laboratory."WBC"). | hgb_mean: average of 'HGB' values for that patient in that month — derived from AVG(Laboratory."HGB"). | plt_sum: sum of 'PLT' values for that patient in that month — derived from SUM(Laboratory."PLT").
params.grounded_columns: Laboratory.ID | Laboratory.Date | Laboratory."T-CHO" | Laboratory."GLU" | Laboratory."WBC" | Laboratory."HGB" | Laboratory."PLT"
params.metric: tcho_sum = SUM(Laboratory."T-CHO") grouped by (Laboratory.ID, strftime('%Y-%m', Laboratory.Date)) | glucose_sum = SUM(Laboratory."GLU") grouped by (Laboratory.ID, strftime('%Y-%m', Laboratory.Date)) | wbc_mean = AVG(Laboratory."WBC") grouped by (Laboratory.ID, strftime('%Y-%m', Laboratory.Date)) | hgb_mean = AVG(Laboratory."HGB") grouped by (Laboratory.ID, strftime('%Y-%m', Laboratory.Date)) | plt_sum = SUM(Laboratory."PLT") grouped by (Laboratory.ID, strftime('%Y-%m', Laboratory.Date))
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to patient_core (or any patient-dimension view/table) on ID — safe because patient_core is one-row-per-patient; patient_monthly_lab_aggregates has at most one row per (ID, month) so its measures will not be duplicated by this join. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a month-dimension table (e.g., calendar months) on month — safe because month is a key for the month dimension; joining does not duplicate measurements as long as the month dimension is one-row-per-month. | NOT safe without care: do NOT directly join this view to any table or view that is one-to-many against (ID, month) (for example: raw Laboratory, examination_events, or any event table that has multiple events per patient-month) without re-aggregation, because such joins will duplicate rows and thus multiply tcho_sum, glucose_sum, plt_sum and distort wbc_mean/hgb_mean. | If you need to combine with a one-to-many child (e.g., multiple exams in the same month), either: (a) aggregate the child to the same (ID, month) grain before joining, or (b) join and then re-aggregate the combined result back to (ID, month) using SUM/AVG as appropriate. This preserves correct measures. | Joining to other AGG/ROLLUP views that are at the same grain (ID, month) is safe — e.g., joining patient_monthly_lab_aggregates to another view aggregated by (ID, month) will not duplicate measures if join keys are (ID, month). | Be cautious when joining to RANK or WIN views that may have multiple rows per (ID, month) (for example per-sample latest lab where ranking is per ID only) — ensure those views are reduced to one-row-per-(ID, month) before joining. | Planner note: this view's declared grain is (ID, month). Any join that preserves a one-to-one or many-to-one relationship from patient_monthly_lab_aggregates to the other side (i.e., the other side is keyed by (ID, month) or (ID) with at most one row per month) will not require recomputation of internal aggregates. Any join that creates a one-to-many from this view to the other side requires re-aggregation to avoid measure inflation.

  l.Date AS Date,

params.description: One-row-per-patient-per-day latest laboratory record (by Date, then GPT, then ALB) — returns the latest GPT and ALB values for each patient for each date.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve the most recent laboratory GPT and ALB values for each patient on each calendar Date. | Compose patient-level time series of latest daily lab values (GPT, ALB) without duplicates for the same patient/date. | Join latest-per-day lab values to patient demographic or exam events when you need exactly one lab row per patient/date. | Aggregate or compute trends per patient/date (e.g., daily change) using the single representative lab row for that day.
params.output_schema: ID: patient identifier — derived from Laboratory.ID | Date: calendar date of the lab record — derived from Laboratory.Date | GPT: measured GPT value from the selected latest lab row — derived from Laboratory.GPT | ALB: measured ALB value from the selected latest lab row — derived from Laboratory.ALB
params.grounded_columns: Laboratory.ID | Laboratory.Date | Laboratory.GPT | Laboratory.ALB
params.metric: lab_row_rank = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY Laboratory.ID, Laboratory.Date ORDER BY Laboratory.Date DESC, Laboratory.GPT DESC, Laboratory.ALB DESC) | GPT = Laboratory.GPT (value from the row with lab_row_rank = 1) | ALB = Laboratory.ALB (value from the row with lab_row_rank = 1)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to patient_core on patient_core.ID = patient_lab_latest_per_day.ID — safe because patient_lab_latest_per_day has at most one row per (ID, Date) and joining to a one-row-per-patient dimension will not duplicate these per-day rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to examination_events on examination_events.ID = patient_lab_latest_per_day.ID and examination_events.Date = patient_lab_latest_per_day.Date ONLY WHEN examination_events is known to be at most one row per (ID, Date); if examination_events contains multiple events per (ID, Date) this will duplicate lab rows. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views such as laboratory_records or exams_with_same_day_lab without first aggregating that target to the same grain (ID, Date) because those are multi-row per (ID, Date) and would multiply this view's rows/measures. Instead, aggregate the many-side (e.g., COUNT(*), MIN/ MAX, or choose a single row via window function) to produce one row per (ID, Date) before joining. | when joining to patient-level aggregates (e.g., lab_aggregates_per_patient or examination_counts_per_patient) that are aggregated to the patient grain (ID), either: (a) join on ID and then re-aggregate patient_lab_latest_per_day up to ID to avoid producing per-day detail, or (b) join patient-level aggregates to a derived subquery that groups patient_lab_latest_per_day to ID. This avoids multiplying lab measures by multiple aggregate rows. | if composing metrics (sums, averages) across this view after joining other tables, ensure the planner aggregates at the output grain you intend (e.g., SUM or AVG over GPT by ID or by Date). Do not rely on row-counts from joins with many-to-one or many-to-many relationships to represent unique lab measures unless the join target has been reduced to one row per (ID, Date). | safe use examples: (1) LEFT JOIN patient_core ON patient_core.ID = patient_lab_latest_per_day.ID — retains one lab row per (ID, Date); (2) Aggregate this view to per-patient: SELECT ID, AVG(GPT) FROM patient_lab_latest_per_day GROUP BY ID — correct patient-level average of daily latest GPT. | unsafe use example: INNER JOIN laboratory_records lr ON lr.ID = patient_lab_latest_per_day.ID AND lr.Date = patient_lab_latest_per_day.Date — unsafe because laboratory_records may contain multiple measurements per (ID, Date) and would multiply the selected latest-per-day rows unless lr is first deduplicated/aggregated.

  COUNT(l.Date) AS matching_lab_count,

params.metric: matching_lab_count = COUNT(Laboratory.Date)  -- count of matched lab rows per patient (null-safe because LEFT JOIN used; yields 0 when no lab rows after outer filters are applied) | latest_matching_lab_date = MAX(Laboratory.Date)  -- most recent lab date among matched lab rows per patient | has_matching_lab = CASE WHEN COUNT(Laboratory.Date) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END  -- boolean indicator derived from the count

This preserves cardinality correctness. | You may safely inner join to views that are explicitly one-row-per-patient (e.g., lab_latest_per_patient, lab_aggregates_per_patient, examination_counts_per_patient) on ID because those do not duplicate patient rows; verify sibling view grains before joining. | When consumers apply additional filters on Laboratory columns, apply them in an outer WHERE (or ON) before grouping so that matching_lab_count and latest_matching_lab_date reflect the filtered set; this view was implemented to allow such external filtering — do not add filters to this view's definition if you want counts restricted by lab attributes.

params.when_to_use: Retrieve laboratory event attributes (ID, Date, GPT) together with the corresponding patient's demographic/diagnosis fields for row-level reporting or filtering. | Filter or group laboratory events by patient attributes (e.g., diagnosis) while keeping event-level grain. | Compose further SQL that aggregates laboratory measures per patient or per date using this view as the laboratory-event detail input.

views.name: patients_with_high_tbili_latest_lab_flag
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.ID AS ID,
  CASE WHEN EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l
    WHERE l.ID = p.ID
      AND l."T-BIL" IS NOT NULL
      AND l."T-BIL" >= 1.2
  ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_tbili_ge_threshold,
  (SELECT MIN(l2.Date) FROM Laboratory l2 WHERE l2.ID = p.ID) AS earliest_lab_date,
  (SELECT MAX(l3.Date) FROM Laboratory l3 WHERE l3.ID = p.ID) AS latest_lab_date
FROM Patient p

params.description: For each patient ID, indicates whether the patient ever had a total bilirubin (T-BIL) >= 1.2, and returns the patient's earliest and latest laboratory dates.
params.when_to_use: Determine which patients have had clinically-elevated T-BIL (>= 1.2) at any time | Filter or flag patient cohorts based on presence/absence of elevated T-BIL | Compose patient-level analyses that need each patient's lab date range (earliest and latest lab dates) | Use as a patient-level input to join with other patient-level views when building higher-level aggregates or cohorts
params.output_schema: ID: patient identifier — derived from Patient.ID (base table Patient, column ID) | has_tbili_ge_threshold: binary flag (1/0) indicating whether any Laboratory row for this patient has T-BIL >= 1.2 — derived from existence test over Laboratory."T-BIL" (base table Laboratory, column "T-BIL") for the same ID | earliest_lab_date: the minimum Laboratory.Date for this patient — derived from MIN(Laboratory.Date) over rows with same ID (base table Laboratory, column Date) | latest_lab_date: the maximum Laboratory.Date for this patient — derived from MAX(Laboratory.Date) over rows with same ID (base table Laboratory, column Date)
params.grounded_columns: Patient.ID | Laboratory.ID | Laboratory."T-BIL" | Laboratory.Date
params.metric: has_tbili_ge_threshold = CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID = Patient.ID AND l."T-BIL" IS NOT NULL AND l."T-BIL" >= 1.2) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END | earliest_lab_date = (SELECT MIN(l2.Date) FROM Laboratory l2 WHERE l2.ID = Patient.ID) | latest_lab_date = (SELECT MAX(l3.Date) FROM Laboratory l3 WHERE l3.ID = Patient.ID)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to patient-level dimensions or views on ID (e.g., patient_core on Patient.ID) — safe because this view has exactly one row per Patient.ID, so patient-level joins will not duplicate its measures. | SAFE: join to patient_with_latest_lab, lab_aggregates_per_patient, examination_counts_per_patient, patients_with_recent_exam_rank, patient_demographic_admission, or any other one-row-per-patient view on ID — these are one-to-one at the patient grain, so measures remain unduplicated. | DO NOT join directly (inner/left) this view to multi-row-per-patient tables or views that are at a finer grain (e.g., Laboratory (raw rows), examination_events, examinations_with_same_day_lab, lab_latest_per_patient if it is per-patient-per-test, or any unaggregated event-level view) without first aggregating or deduplicating the many-side to one row per patient — doing so will multiply this view's boolean/aggregate semantics and produce incorrect counts/sums. | If you must combine with a one-to-many table (for example to analyze per-lab-row results together with this patient-level flag), do one of the following: (a) aggregate the one-to-many table to patient-level first (e.g., MIN(Date), MAX(Date), COUNT(*), AVG(...)) and then join on ID; or (b) join and then re-aggregate at patient-level (e.g., GROUP BY ID) to avoid duplicating the has_tbili_ge_threshold flag or date range. | Explanation why joins to one-to-many would duplicate: this view's measures (has_tbili_ge_threshold, earliest_lab_date, latest_lab_date) are computed per patient. Joining a patient-level row to N laboratory/event rows will repeat the same patient-level values N times, which will incorrectly inflate measures if aggregated without re-aggregation. | Notes about NULLs and absence of labs: patients with no Laboratory rows will have has_tbili_ge_threshold = 0 (because EXISTS is false) and earliest_lab_date / latest_lab_date = NULL (because MIN/MAX over no rows yields NULL). Treat NULL dates explicitly when composing time-window filters or date arithmetic.
